title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Earnestly Studying and Implementing the Negotiable Instruments Law and the Security Law
keywords_en: contract dispute; negotiable instrument; guarantee; application for retrial
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court Notice on Diligently Studying and Implementing the Negotiable Instruments Law and the Guarantee Law

Fa Fa [1995] No. 19

All High People's Courts of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army:

The Negotiable Instruments Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Negotiable Instruments Law) and the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Guarantee Law) have been adopted at the 13th Session and the 14th Session of the Standing Committee of the Eighth National People's Congress, respectively, and shall come into effect on January 1, 1996 and October 1, 1995, respectively. For the correct application of the Negotiable Instruments Law and the Guarantee Law in adjudication work, the following notice is hereby given regarding the study and implementation of the Negotiable Instruments Law and the Guarantee Law:

1. People's courts at all levels shall actively organize adjudicators to diligently study the Negotiable Instruments Law and the Guarantee Law, accurately grasp the legislative intent, deeply comprehend the meaning of each provision, and fully understand the positive role of the Negotiable Instruments Law in regulating negotiable instrument acts, protecting the legitimate rights and interests of parties to negotiable instrument activities, combating negotiable instrument fraud crimes, and maintaining socio-economic order; the role of the Guarantee Law in promoting capital financing and commodity circulation and in securing the realization of creditor's rights; and the positive impact of these two important laws in promoting the development of the socialist market economy.

2. Adjudicators shall, through their adjudicative activities in cases involving negotiable instrument disputes and guarantee contract disputes, correctly apply the law, and in conjunction with case handling, use cases to explain the law, and shall pay attention to utilizing forms such as open trials and news media to vigorously publicize the Negotiable Instruments Law, the Guarantee Law, and their significance, and to educate citizens to enhance their awareness of negotiable instruments and guarantees and to consciously abide by the law.

3. For negotiable instrument acts and guarantee acts that occurred prior to the effectiveness of the Negotiable Instruments Law and the Guarantee Law, the relevant provisions in effect at the time of such acts shall apply; if there were no provisions at the time of the act, the provisions of the Negotiable Instruments Law and the Guarantee Law may be referenced by analogy.

For cases involving negotiable instrument disputes and guarantee disputes where a party applies for retrial of a legally effective judgment rendered before the effectiveness of the Negotiable Instruments Law and the Guarantee Law, or where a decision is made to retry such a case pursuant to trial supervision procedures, the relevant provisions in effect at the time shall still apply.

4. After the effectiveness of the Negotiable Instruments Law and the Guarantee Law, any judicial interpretations on matters concerning negotiable instruments and guarantees made by the Supreme People's Court prior to the promulgation of these two laws shall, to the extent they conflict with the Negotiable Instruments Law and the Guarantee Law, except as provided in item 3 of this notice, no longer apply.

5. In the process of implementing the Negotiable Instruments Law and the Guarantee Law, people's courts at all levels shall pay attention to summarizing trial practice experience, strengthen investigation and research, and earnestly ensure the effective implementation of the laws. For difficult issues concerning the application of law arising in the trial of cases, solutions or preferred opinions shall be submitted to this Court for reference when formulating judicial interpretations.

August 30, 1995
